Let <MATH_0001> and <MATH_0002> be irreducible schemes.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> We say <MATH_0003> and <MATH_0004> are <TEXTITOPEN_0001>birational<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if <MATH_0005> and <MATH_0006> are isomorphic
in the category of irreducible schemes and dominant rational maps.
<STRUCT_0003> Assume <MATH_0007> and <MATH_0008> are schemes over a base scheme <MATH_0009>.
We say <MATH_0010> and <MATH_0011> are <TEXTITOPEN_0002><MATH_0012>-birational<TEXTITCLOSE_0002> if <MATH_0013> and <MATH_0014> are
isomorphic in the category of irreducible schemes over <MATH_0015> and
dominant <MATH_0016>-rational maps.
<STRUCT_0004>

<STRUCT_0001>
If <MATH_0001> and <MATH_0002> are birational irreducible schemes, then the set of rational
maps from <MATH_0003> to <MATH_0004> is bijective with the set of rational map from <MATH_0005> to <MATH_0006>
for all schemes <MATH_0007> (functorially in <MATH_0008>). For ``general'' irreducible schemes
this is just one possible definition. Another would be
to require <MATH_0009> and <MATH_0010> have isomorphic rings of rational functions. For
varieties these conditions are equivalent, see
Lemma <REF_0001>.

Let <MATH_0001> and <MATH_0002> be irreducible schemes.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> The schemes <MATH_0003> and <MATH_0004> are birational if and only if they have
isomorphic nonempty opens.
<STRUCT_0003> Assume <MATH_0005> and <MATH_0006> are schemes over a base scheme <MATH_0007>. Then
<MATH_0008> and <MATH_0009> are <MATH_0010>-birational if and only if there are nonempty
opens <MATH_0011> and <MATH_0012> which are <MATH_0013>-isomorphic.
<STRUCT_0004>
